main.title: 4월 수출 859억달러 '역대 최대'…반도체·SSD, 美·中 수출 ↑
main.body:
South Korea achieved record April exports of $85.89 billion (한화 약 117조 원), representing a 48% increase year-over-year. The nation simultaneously surpassed $80 billion in monthly exports and $20 billion in trade surplus for two consecutive months — a historic first.

Semiconductors emerged as the primary growth driver, with exports surging 173.5% to $31.9 billion (약 43.6조 원). This marked the 13th consecutive month of record performance for April shipments. The sector benefited from global AI infrastructure expansion, creating excess demand for both NAND and DRAM products.

The computer storage sector (SSDs) experienced extraordinary growth of 515.8%, driven by surging datacenter demand from AI proliferation.

China led regional growth with exports up 62.5% extending a six-month positive streak. United States exports climbed 54% to $163 billion.

Semiconductors now account for more than 37% of total Korean export value, with High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and enterprise SSD products as primary contributors.
main.keep_reason: Korean April exports record with semiconductor +173.5% and SSD +515.8% — primary market intelligence on AI infrastructure demand driving Korean semi.
main.select_reason: Historic Korean export record with semiconductor +173.5% / SSD +515.8% — pace-setting macro signal for AI infra demand and primary national market intelligence.

main.title: OpenAI missed revenue and user targets, faces internal concern over meeting data center spend commitments — report
main.body:
OpenAI has missed revenue and user targets and faces internal concern over its ability to meet data center infrastructure spending commitments as the company reworks Stargate and prepares for an IPO, according to a report.

The company is reworking its $500 billion (약 685조 원) Stargate initiative, shifting from a fixed data center joint venture toward a more flexible strategy for securing computing capacity.

OpenAI has effectively abandoned the joint-venture structure in favor of a string of major bilateral agreements. Oracle is playing the lead role with its pledge to supply 4.5 gigawatts of compute capacity over five years. AMD, Broadcom, Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Cerebras have also signed partnerships.

Despite the strategic changes, OpenAI insists the overall strategy remains intact, claiming it has already secured more than 8 gigawatts of capacity toward an initial target of 10 gigawatts by 2030, and is now aiming for more than $600 billion (약 820조 원) in total investment.

Microsoft agreed to rent data center capacity at a site in Norway that was initially intended for OpenAI and marketed as part of the Stargate initiative, reflecting the evolving and flexible nature of the programme.
main.keep_reason: OpenAI Stargate rework with bilateral deals across Oracle/AMD/Broadcom/Nvidia/CoreWeave/Cerebras — defines hyperscaler infrastructure landscape.
main.select_reason: $500B→$600B Stargate reframe and 8GW-of-10GW progress redraws hyperscaler infra map; defines AMD/Broadcom/Cerebras silicon procurement landscape MangoBoost lives in.

main.title: 2조 규모 '국가 AI컴퓨팅 센터' 참여 자격 까다로워져 '논란'
main.body:
South Korea's 2 trillion won (약 2조 원) National AI Computing Center faces mounting criticism over increasingly stringent participation requirements for private companies, according to reporting from THE ELEC.

The government mandates that participating firms must: secure GPU supply commitments from NVIDIA and AMD through written agreements, achieve a 50% domestic AI chip ratio by 2030, build computing capacity of at least 1 exaflop (FP32 standard), and continuously upgrade domestic semiconductors annually.

Industry observers characterize these conditions as unrealistic. The special-purpose company will secure approximately 400 billion won (약 4,000억 원) in capital over six years — enough to cover only about 11,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs, when 16,667 units are required for minimum capacity targets.

Two domestic AI chip developers face qualification obstacles: Rebellions' Atom NPU shows promise with 3rd generation Revel sampling planned, but concerns persist about achieving H100-equivalent performance levels. FuriosaAI's Renegade NPU reportedly achieved performance comparable to older A100 GPUs rather than current H100 standards. Meta's past acquisition proposal also complicates FuriosaAI's domestic classification.

Timeline: Technical and policy evaluation in June, selection of preferred negotiating partner in August-September.
main.keep_reason: 국가 AI 컴퓨팅 센터 참여 요건 강화로 Rebellions·FuriosaAI 자격 논란 — 핵심 한국 AI 인프라 정책 프로젝트.
main.select_reason: Korean sovereign-AI flagship policy with hard qualification numbers; Rebellions/Furiosa exposure plus AMD GPU written-commitment clause directly touches MangoBoost's home market.

main.title: Prediction: This Will Be the Top-Performing AI Semiconductor Stock Over the Next Year (Hint: It's Not Nvidia, Broadcom, or Micron)
main.body:
Motley Fool argues that Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) will outperform better-known competitors like Nvidia, Broadcom, and Micron over the next year, driven by its under-the-radar role in AI data center infrastructure.

Marvell designs high-speed Ethernet switches, network interface cards, and data processing units (DPUs) that optimize data movement within AI data centers. Three major catalysts support this thesis:

1. Nvidia Partnership — a $2 billion (약 2.7조 원) strategic investment and collaboration will accelerate development of next-generation Ethernet switches and DPUs optimized for Nvidia's AI platforms.

2. Hyperscaler Spending Shift — with $720 billion (약 985조 원) in AI capex expected from major tech companies, spending is shifting from training (Nvidia's domain) toward inference, where Marvell's low-power inference engines provide advantages.

3. Google TPU Talks — Google is in discussions with Marvell for two new AI chips: a memory processing unit and a new inference-focused TPU, adding to Marvell's existing custom silicon contracts with Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta.

Unlike Nvidia's $5 trillion valuation, Marvell has a smaller market cap with greater room for earnings surprises. Marvell data center revenue reached $6.1 billion (약 8.3조 원) in fiscal 2026.
main.keep_reason: Marvell DPU and inference SmartNIC role plus $2B Nvidia partnership and Google TPU talks — direct DPU competitor intelligence.
main.select_reason: Direct DPU competitor briefing with $2B NVIDIA partnership, Google MPU/TPU talks, and inference-spend pivot — highest MangoBoost employee notability of the day.

main.title: Cloudflare Builds High-Performance Infrastructure for Running LLMs
main.body:
Cloudflare has unveiled new infrastructure designed to operate large language models (LLMs) across its global network, addressing key challenges posed by computationally expensive AI systems through innovative architectural approaches.

Disaggregated Prefill Architecture: Cloudflare separates LLM request processing into two specialized stages. One machine handles input token processing and key-value cache population (compute-intensive prefill stage), while another manages output token generation (memory-intensive decode stage). As the engineering team explains: 'Prefill is usually compute bound, while decode is memory bound.'

Custom Inference Engine — Infire: This custom engine optimizes multi-GPU model execution, improves efficiency, reduces memory consumption, and accelerates model startup times. The system employs pipeline and tensor parallelism to balance throughput and latency effectively.

Ultra-large models like Kimi K2.5 (exceeding 1 trillion parameters, approximately 560GB) require distribution across multiple GPUs. Running such models demands at least eight H100 graphics processing units simply to load parameters into memory.

Cloudflare has also introduced Unweight, a compression system claiming 15-22% reduction in model weights without accuracy loss, enabling faster and more efficient inference globally.
main.keep_reason: Disaggregated prefill/decode architecture with custom Infire inference engine and Unweight compression — central to MangoBoost's AI infrastructure value-add domain.
main.select_reason: Cloudflare productionizing disaggregated prefill/decode + custom Infire engine maps directly onto MangoBoost's disaggregated-inference value prop — high employee attention.

main.title: Google Is A Full Stack AI Player, And Is Playing Well
main.body:
Google delivered strong Q1 2026 results demonstrating the advantages of its vertically integrated AI strategy spanning custom silicon (TPUs, Ironwood), infrastructure, platform services, and consumer applications.

Google Cloud achieved 63% year-on-year growth to reach $20.02 billion (약 27.4조 원) in Q1 2026, dramatically exceeding analyst forecasts of $18.05 billion. Google's CEO indicated the company is compute constrained in the near term, with cloud demand exceeding available capacity. The company's cloud backlog reached over $460 billion (약 630조 원), nearly doubling the previous quarter.

Google's latest TPU, Ironwood, is described as the first Google TPU for the age of inference. The company is also in talks with Marvell Technology to develop additional custom AI inference chips alongside its existing Broadcom TPU programme, diversifying its silicon supply chain.

Alphabet raised its capex guidance to $180-$190 billion (약 246-260조 원) for 2026, reflecting the scale of investment required to maintain compute infrastructure leadership.

The article positions Google as uniquely advantaged by having in-house silicon, data centers, hyperscale cloud, and consumer AI products — a stack few competitors can match end-to-end.
main.keep_reason: Google Cloud +63% with Ironwood TPU and Marvell custom silicon talks — hyperscaler in-house silicon strategy and $460B backlog signal demand.
main.select_reason: Google Cloud +63% with $460B backlog and Ironwood inference-TPU strategy plus Marvell silicon talks — hyperscaler vertical-integration story shaping AI infra demand.

main.title: MOREH Demonstrates Production-Ready LLM Inference on Tenstorrent Galaxy, Achieving DGX A100-Class Performance with Improved Cost Efficiency
main.body:
Moreh, an AI infrastructure software company, announced that it has successfully validated LLM (Large Language Model) inference performance on the Tenstorrent Galaxy Wormhole system using its proprietary MoAI Inference Framework. Based on tests across leading Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models — including GPT-OSS, Qwen, GLM, and DeepSeek — Moreh achieved LLM inference performance on Tenstorrent Galaxy Wormhole matching or surpassing NVIDIA DGX A100-class systems.

MoAI Inference Framework is a disaggregated inference solution that enables unified operation of heterogeneous GPUs and NPUs — including NVIDIA, AMD, and Tenstorrent — within a single cluster, allowing enterprises to build flexible AI infrastructure strategies without vendor lock-in.

Moreh improved cost efficiency by implementing a disaggregated serving architecture that combines GPUs with Tenstorrent Wormhole chips, utilizing Tenstorrent processors as dedicated prefill accelerators to reduce reliance on high-cost HBM and lower overall infrastructure costs.

Moreh is developing its own core AI infrastructure engine and, through its foundation LLM subsidiary Motif Technologies, is building end-to-end capabilities spanning both infrastructure and model domains. The company collaborates with AMD, Tenstorrent, and SGLang as key partners.
main.keep_reason: Tier-1 competitor Moreh + Tenstorrent disaggregated serving with prefill accelerators — directly competes with MangoBoost's core disaggregated inference value proposition.
main.select_reason: Tier-1 competitor Moreh productionizing disaggregated prefill on Tenstorrent — directly contests MangoBoost's value prop; warrants full TLDR not just competitor bullet.

main.title: 컴퓨팅 확보 비상 걸린 앤트로픽, 영국 칩 신예와 파트너십 검토
main.body:
Anthropic is urgently seeking new AI chip sources beyond its existing suppliers. The company is in discussions with British startup Fractile regarding next-generation inference chips, according to reporting from The Information.

Fractile, founded in 2022 and emerging from stealth mode in mid-2024, represents an unconventional choice for Anthropic. The startup lacks extensive hardware manufacturing experience, yet Anthropic is actively negotiating chip procurement despite this risk. Fractile's chips are expected to become available as early as next year (2027).

Anthropic faces severe computing resource constraints due to surging demand for AI coding and automation tasks. Users report service disruptions and consumption limits that developers are contesting.

Successfully contracting with Fractile would strengthen Anthropic's negotiating position with major suppliers including Google, Amazon, and Nvidia. Fractile and competitors emphasize efficient inference capabilities through SRAM-based architectures that minimize data movement, reducing costs and power consumption.

Anthropic is also reportedly reviewing designs for proprietary inference chips — a strategy OpenAI and Meta are pursuing. The shift reflects growing industry momentum away from Nvidia's GPU dominance in inference workloads.
main.keep_reason: Anthropic의 Fractile 등 SRAM 기반 추론 칩 다변화 검토 — AI 추론 칩 공급/효율 이슈와 NVIDIA 의존 탈피 시그널.
main.select_reason: Anthropic shopping SRAM-based inference startups (Fractile) plus own-chip review — concrete signal of NVIDIA-decoupling momentum that frames MangoBoost's market opportunity.

competitor_articles.title: The Second Time Will Be The IPO Charm For Cerebras
competitor_articles.body:
Cerebras Systems is making another push to go public after withdrawing its initial IPO filing from September 2024. The company, which creates waferscale AI chips, is pursuing a second IPO in April 2026 with significantly improved financial prospects and major customer deals.

The company raised $1.1 billion in Series G funding (October 2025) at an $8.1 billion valuation, followed by $1 billion in Series H funding in February 2026, pushing valuation to $23 billion (약 31.5조 원).

In January 2026, Cerebras secured a transformative agreement potentially worth up to $20 billion (약 27.4조 원) with OpenAI, with an initial 750-megawatt installation through 2028 and options for 3 gigawatts in 2029-2030. The deal includes a $1 billion working capital loan.

March 2026 brought a binding term sheet pairing Cerebras CS-3 systems with AWS's Trainium AI infrastructure across multiple years for global distribution.

Cerebras now has $510 million (약 6,980억 원) in annual revenue with multiple substantial customers. The article also notes that Nvidia 'acquihired' most of Groq for an enormous $20 billion (약 27.4조 원) to add low-latency inference capabilities — intensifying competition for alternative inference solutions.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: Cerebras IPO push at $23B valuation plus $20B OpenAI deal and AWS Trainium pairing — major competitor financial event with Nvidia/Groq acquihire context.

competitor_articles.title: Tenstorrent's Galaxy Blackhole AI servers are finally out
competitor_articles.body:
Tenstorrent announced the general availability of its Galaxy Blackhole AI compute platform. Each 6U system contains 32 Blackhole accelerators connected via 100 Tbps of aggregate bandwidth in a dense Ethernet mesh configuration.

A single Galaxy system delivers: 1 TB of GDDR6 memory, 16 TB/s of memory bandwidth, and 23 petaFLOPS of dense FP8 performance, all priced at $110,000 (약 1.5억 원). For comparison, NVIDIA's eight-way DGX boxes cost between three and five times as much.

The architecture supports clustering. Tenstorrent's base Galaxy Supercluster costs $440,000 and comprises four Blackhole systems; the design accommodates up to 144 nodes with over 4,000 chips total.

For large language models like DeepSeek V3, a four-node Blackhole Galaxy Supercluster can process a 100,000 token prompt in less than four seconds. The system generates up to 300 tokens per second per user, with expectations to reach 350 through software improvements.

Several datacenter providers are adopting the hardware, including Cirrascale, Equinix, and Japan's ai&. The TT-Deploy event on May 1 shared additional deployment details.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: Tier-2 competitor Tenstorrent Galaxy Blackhole GA at $110K vs DGX 3-5x cheaper, 100Tbps Ethernet mesh — direct alternative to NVIDIA inference platforms.

competitor_articles.title: AI Inferencing Will Define 2026, and the Market's Wide Open
competitor_articles.body:
2026 is shaping up to be the breakout year of AI inferencing — the process where a trained machine learning model generates predictions and outputs from new input data. The inference market is wide open with no dominant player in the way NVIDIA dominates training.

Multiple architectures are competing: waferscale (Cerebras), RISC-V (Tenstorrent), LPDDR-based LPU (HyperAccel, Groq), NPU (Rebellions, FuriosaAI), and custom ASIC (AWS Trainium, Google TPU, Microsoft Maia).

The economics of inference differ fundamentally from training. Training happens once; inference runs continuously at scale. The winner will optimize for cost-per-token, latency, and power efficiency — not raw FLOPS.

FriendliAI, which builds inference software optimizations including speculative decoding and continuous batching, is expanding its platform to cover more complex inference pipelines including multi-agent workloads.

NVIDIA is responding with inference-specific products including its NIM microservices and inference-optimized Hopper and Blackwell configurations, but specialists argue architecture-level advantages for purpose-built inference chips remain significant for power-constrained deployments.
